question.text: English forces under Henry V utilized the longbow during this battle, which took place during St. Crispin's Day. During this battle, French forces under Charles d'Albret got stuck in muddy terrain.
question.clue: One side in this battle copied a tactic used by the Ottomans at the battle of Nicopolis.

swap.leadin: Give the following about a French religious group.
swap.text: The Edict of Saint-Germain was passed by Queen Catherine de Medici in 1572. It guaranteed private worship by this group of French Protestants.
swap.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

question.text: This first Bourbon king of France was a Huguenot, but he converted to Catholicism in order to be king. Referring to his conversion, he supposedly said, "Paris is well worth a mass."
question.answerHtml: Henry IV of France (accept Henry III of Navarre; do not accept Henry IV of Navarre or Henry III of France)
question.clue: Days afterwards, Gaspard de Coligny was murdered in the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre.

swap.leadin: Name the following leaders of France.
swap.text: This Prime Minister of France, known as "the Tiger," led the French delegation at the Paris Peace Conference. His insistence on harsh German reparations made it into the Treaty of Versailles.
swap.clue: During the Dreyfus affair, this man published Emile Zola's J'Accuse letter on the front of his newspaper, L'Aurore.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated Odo of Aquitaine at the Battle of Soissons, though he later fought alongside Odo against an Umayyad invasion led by Abd-ar-Rahman.
question.text: Identify this ruler who defeated a Muslim army at the Battle of Tours. This ruler's son Pepin the Short became a king following the deposition of Childeric III.
question.clue: He served as Mayor of the Palace in Austrasia, a title he passed to his son, Pepin III after securing another victory at the Battle of Cologne.

swap.leadin: This woman supported her son, Henry the Young King, in a revolt against her husband, Henry II, leading to her imprisonment.
swap.text: Name this woman, the mother of Richard the Lionheart and King John of England.
swap.answerHtml: Eleanor of Aquitaine [or Eleanor of Guyenne; or Eleonore d'Aquitaine; or Alienor d'Aquitaine]
swap.clue: According to Andreas Capellanus, the "Court of Love" at Poitiers was where this person and Countess Marie of Champagne taught chivalry.

question.text: In this 1870 battle, General von Moltke surrounded and captured Napoleon III's troops, winning the Franco-Prussian War.
question.clue: Attempts at withdrawal by the losing side were thwarted by heavy enemy artillery fire from Krupp-made cannons.

swap.text: After decades of war, the Carolingians were succeeded in Western Francia by this dynasty. Later French dynasties, like the Bourbons, are distant branches of this family founded by Hugh.
swap.answerHtml: The Capetian Dynasty [or Capet House; prompt “House of France”] <SJW>
swap.clue: Another king of this dynasty was captured by Edward the Black Prince and was ransomed after the battle of Poitiers.

question.text: This first president of the French Third Republic was propped up by "liberation loans" from the Rothschilds. This rival of Francois Guizot had previously served under Louis-Philippe.
question.clue: As a historian, this leader published a major history of the French Revolution in 1827, which praised the Revolution of 1789 but criticized the Reign of Terror.

swap.leadin: This president introduced both private television channels and proportional representation for Parlement in a failed attempt to maintain his party's legislative majority.
swap.text: Name this politician who later appointed Edith Cresson as his country's first female prime minister.
swap.clue: This leader of the Socialist Party opposed the founding of the Fifth Republic, and he ordered the sinking of the Greenpeace vessel Rainbow Warrior.

question.leadin: This city is home to a Roman amphitheatre and the Maison Caree, a well-preserved Roman temple.
question.text: Name this city in Southern France whose name is the origin of the name of a very common form of cloth.
question.clue: This city contains the best preserved Roman amphitheater in the world, as well as an almost completely intact Roman Temple, the Maison Carree, which now contains a tacky 3-D theater.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about World War One battles.
swap.text: The attack of this French fortified city in February 1916 was initially a success for Falkenhayn's German forces. However, the French under Petain mounted a heroic defense of the city, whose only remaining supply line was called the "Sacred Way."
swap.clue: At a battle near this city, Charles Mangin retook Forts Vaux and Douaumont, and defenders received supplies along the Sacred Way.

question.leadin: This treaty followed the battles of Saint-Quentin and Gravelines, and it transferred land to Emmanuel-Philibert.
question.text: Name this 1559 treaty, which confirmed Spanish control of much of Italy and was signed by Henry II of France.
question.clue: Prior to signing this treaty, one monarch who was party to it sent a memorandum to his sister Joanna claiming that his presence in Flanders was necessary to prevent a possible invasion of England.

swap.text: Before France completely fell apart, it achieved historic reforms under this left-wing government headed by Leon Blum. This government signed the Matignon Accords, which guaranteed a 40-hour work week.
swap.clue: Meetings that this government conducted with trade unions resulted in the Matignon accords, which granted a 40-hour work week.

question.leadin: The Duke of Brunswick was mortally wounded at this battle, where a young Carl von Clausewitz was captured.
question.text: Name this 1806 battle at which Marshal Davout ("da-VOO") routed a numerically superior Prussian army. This battle is often paired with Napoleon's victory at nearby Jena ("YAY-na").

swap.leadin: Answer the following about political changes in the year 2012.
swap.text: This far right-wing party's candidate in the French 2012 elections, Marine Le Pen, received eighteen percent of the vote in the first round, falling behind Francois Hollande and Nicolas Sarkozy. It is the third-largest political party in France.
swap.clue: Marine Le Pen will stand for this ultra-right-wing party, which her father Jean-Marie founded. Her rhetoric has been anti-European and anti-immigration, but she has tried to distance her party from extremism.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about a French monarch and his reign.
question.text: This son of Blanche of Castile repelled revolts by Raymond VII of Toulouse and eventually signed a treaty of Paris with Henry III of England.
question.clue: This king of France who led the Seventh and Eighth Crusades.

swap.text: France's loss to Prussia sparked this movement aimed at regaining land lost during the war, such as Alsace ("ahl-sahss") and Lorraine. Georges Boulanger ("zhorzh boo-lawn-zhay") was nicknamed this movement's "General ("zheh-neh-rahl")" for his inveterate support of it.
swap.clue: This political ideology represented by Albert Bettanier's The Black Spot. Georges Ernest Boulanger was nicknamed General [this ideology].

question.leadin: Answer the following about traditional European forms of transhumance, the practice of moving livestock between fixed winter and summer pastures.
question.text: This historian's book Feudal Society discusses cycles of transhumance and nomadism in European history. His book The Royal Touch analyzes the medieval European belief that monarchs could cure diseases like scrofula.

swap.text: The father of all commentary on Lamentations, as with the Tanach as a whole, is this 11th and 12th Century French Rabbi.
